correctness.rationale: For one-dimensional Dirichlet Poisson tridiagonal A_n=tridiag(-1,2,-1), initial x0=0 and nonnegative isolated load plus remote symmetric hat, the exact 2D Galerkin formula x2=[(m0m3-m1m2)b-(m0m2-m1²)Ab]/D, D=m1m3-m2²>0, gives the first-coordinate numerator rN_k(r)/D for a two-peak plateau. The exact polynomial is N_k(r)=2r⁴-2r³+A_kr²-B_kr-C_k with stated cubic k-coefficients. C_k>0, N_k(1)=2(k+1)(4k-5)>0, and second derivative of N_k>0 for all r≥0,k≥2; with the derivative of N_k at zero<0, this proves a UNIQUE positive zero r_k∈(0,1) and sign negative below, positive above. Uniform k^-3 expansion and Taylor at 1 establish r_k=1-2/k+O(k^-2). One-peak hat instead has lim_{r↓0} x2_1/r=k/3>0; plateau has strictly negative limit. Independently reconstructed Krylov moments and exact two-step CG for k=2,3,4,7,10,25, rational amplitudes and padding; integer b=(1,0,0,2,4,4,2,0,..) gives x2_1=-58/171. Green matrix A^-1 has strictly positive entries so exact solution remains positive. Checks are finite witnesses only; analytic moments/proof cover all n≥required and k≥2.

originality.rationale: The published general result that CG can become negative even for Stieltjes matrices, and that three dimensions suffice, is explicitly prior work. The earlier Resultary finding proves a sharp *different* 3x3 threshold at diagonal parameter a=4 for forcing b_B; it does not imply the parity-dependent remote discrete-hat profile for the canonical unmodified Poisson A_n (all diagonal 2), exact unique amplitude threshold r_k, asymptotics or opposite small-amplitude sign between one- and two-peak hats. Beckermann–Kuijlaars analyze exact same Poisson finite-difference matrix but special-RHS convergence rates, not transient component sign frontier. Schmelzer–Stoll accessible abstract states general nonnegativity loss, but complete full text remained inaccessible; this is a residual risk, not automatic O failure.
residual_risks: Schmelzer–Stoll 2026 full text was not accessible and may contain specialized examples; abstract alone cannot establish whole-document noncoverage.
Finite exact recurrence checks do not prove arbitrary k; the all-k conclusion depends on the analytic moment and convexity calculation.
The single-peak comparison is only as isolated amplitude tends to zero, not a full all-amplitude classification.

value.rationale: An exact transient sign frontier for a canonical inverse-positive SPD discretization is a motivated finite-element/elliptic-solver question: a simple parity change in a remote nonnegative hat flips the sign of the second CG step at another site while true A^-1 b stays positive. Unique amplitude threshold for all hat widths and asymptotic law are new natural structural facts, not merely one tiny negative witness or unmotivated exact arithmetic.
